name: Navigating the Path to Nursing: Gideon Nyoike's Story

content.title: Navigating the Path to Nursing: Gideon Nyoike's Story
content.summary: Despite the bumpy ride, Gideon looks forward to clinical rotations and making a difference

content.text: As the inaugural cohort of AKU's Bachelor of Science in Nursing - Direct Entry programme advances into their second year, Gideon Nyoike's story offers an inspiring look into the journey of becoming a nurse.

Gideon began his nursing education with curiosity and a hint of uncertainty, expecting a smooth path. "I expected an easy journey, something uncomplicated," he recalls. But as the coursework deepened, he quickly realized that nursing was far more challenging than he had anticipated.

Nursing wasn't Gideon's first choice; he initially dreamed of careers in aviation and medicine. However, conversations with practicing nurses shifted his perspective, revealing the profound impact and depth of the profession. His first year at AKU was a whirlwind of highs and lows. The transition from the structured environment of high school to the self-directed nature of university life was particularly tough. "I had a hard time moving from a system where I was closely supervised to one where I had to handle everything on my own," Gideon reflects. Yet, through persistence and adaptability, he gradually found his footing.

The supportive environment at AKU played a pivotal role in easing his transition. Faculty and staff were approachable and always willing to assist, which made navigating the complexities of his first year more manageable. Among the most rewarding aspects of his experience was patient interaction. "Providing care and a safe place for patients is quite fulfilling," Gideon shares. This hands-on experience has given him a deep sense of purpose and satisfaction.

Outside the classroom, Gideon found camaraderie and balance through his involvement in the AKU football club, a passion that has been with him since childhood. The friendships and shared experiences on the field provided him with a supportive community.

Looking ahead, Gideon is eager to begin clinical rotations and apply his knowledge in real-world settings. His advice to new nursing students is clear: "See the course through. Once you start, there is no turning back. Keep moving forward despite the challenges."
